concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor conceded the record does not resolve materiality and provided no new admissible evidence that the paid pilot commitments are out of scope or that the limitation was resolved, disclosed, or accepted.
The Actor expressly conceded there is no final legal clearance. That narrows the claim but does not close the unresolved legal/policy predicate.
The Actor expressly conceded there is no admissible evidence of disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Monitoring and caveated framing do not satisfy the policy requirement.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record into a narrower, caveated position. That clarification is analytically useful but not evidentiary. The governing policy states that a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the admissible record shows the affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, legal review on disclosure remains open, and there is no admissible evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch. Because those policy predicates remain unsatisfied, the certification position remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats. Caveats can narrow an overbroad rationale, but they do not cure an unmet disclosure-or-acceptance requirement.
remaining_concerns: Materiality remains established because the affected small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, and no admissible evidence shows those commitments are out of launch scope.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so a policy predicate is still unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance as required by policy for a material limitation.
Aggregate readiness above threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate disclosure-or-acceptance requirement.
